presentingComplaint: Large-volume haematemesis and black tarry stools for 6 hours with light-headedness on standing
history: Two episodes of fresh-blood and coffee-ground vomiting since morning, followed by passage of foul black tarry stool. Reports near-syncope on standing. Known alcohol-related cirrhosis (Child-Pugh B) diagnosed 2 years ago on surveillance; prior endoscopy showed grade II-III oesophageal varices. Ongoing daily alcohol intake (~180 g/day), no NSAID use, not on beta-blocker. No prior variceal bleed. Increasing abdominal girth over recent weeks.
examination: Alert but anxious, cool clammy peripheries. Pallor. Stigmata of chronic liver disease: spider naevi, palmar erythema, gynaecomastia. Moderate ascites with shifting dullness, no rebound. Splenomegaly. No asterixis at present; oriented. PR: melaena on glove. No focal source of upper GI bleeding externally.
imaging: Bedside USG abdomen: coarse nodular shrunken liver, splenomegaly, moderate ascites, patent portal vein with hepatopetal flow. No focal mass.
microbiology: Blood cultures and ascitic diagnostic tap sent to exclude SBP; results pending
differentialDiagnoses: Gastric variceal / portal hypertensive gastropathy bleed
finalDiagnosis: Acute oesophageal variceal bleeding on background alcohol-related cirrhosis
citations: Harrison 22e - Cirrhosis and Its Complications / Approach to the Patient with GI Bleeding
AASLD Portal Hypertensive Bleeding in Cirrhosis 2016 (Baveno VII Consensus 2022)
stewardship: Not applicable as primary therapy; however guideline-mandated short-course prophylactic antibiotic (IV ceftriaxone 1 g daily up to 7 days) is standard adjunct in cirrhotic GI bleeding to reduce infection, rebleeding and mortality. Definitive management is vasoactive drug (terlipressin/octreotide), urgent endoscopic band ligation within 12 h, and restrictive transfusion (Hb target ~7-8 g/dL).
contraindications: Terlipressin caution in ischaemic heart disease / peripheral vascular disease
Avoid over-transfusion (Hb >9) - raises portal pressure and rebleeding
Ceftriaxone: adjust/avoid with biliary sludge; use quinolone alternative only if low local resistance
edgeCases: Isolated gastric fundal (IGV1) varices need cyanoacrylate glue, not banding
Urea:creatinine disproportion and normal AST:ALT can mask ongoing bleed; a normal early Hb does not exclude major loss
Consider TIPS as pre-emptive rescue in Child-Pugh B with active bleeding at endoscopy or Child-Pugh C
expectedMaiK: Classic acute variceal bleed in decompensated cirrhosis with haemodynamic instability. Prioritise airway protection and resuscitation, start vasoactive drug and prophylactic ceftriaxone immediately, adopt a restrictive transfusion strategy, and arrange urgent endoscopic band ligation within 12 hours.
